config.title: Night Trains from Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Where the sleepers from Berlin actually go, which station they leave from, what they cost, and which mistakes to avoid.

items.q: Which cities can you reach by night train from Berlin?
items.a: Direct sleepers run to **Vienna and Budapest (nightly, around 20:11)**, **Basel and Zurich (nightly, 20:48)**, **Paris (Mon/Wed/Fri, 17:25)**, **Brussels and Amsterdam (Tue/Thu/Sun, 23:01)**, and **Stockholm** with two trains: the RDC EuroNight on Monday and Friday and the Snälltåget most nights until early November. There is no proper sleeper to Warsaw; use the day EC trains.

items.q: Is there still a night train from Berlin to Paris?
items.a: Yes, but it changed hands. The **ÖBB Nightjet to Paris stopped in December 2025** when France ended its funding. **European Sleeper relaunched the route in March 2026**: it leaves **Berlin Gesundbrunnen at 17:25 on Monday, Wednesday and Friday** and arrives at Paris Nord at 11:28 the next day, via Hamburg and Brussels.

items.q: Which Berlin station do night trains leave from?
items.a: The Nightjet and EuroNight trains to Vienna, Budapest, Basel and Zurich leave from **Berlin Hauptbahnhof**, normally from the lower-level tracks 1 to 8. The **European Sleeper trains to Paris, Brussels and Amsterdam use Berlin Gesundbrunnen**, one Ringbahn stop north of the centre. Check the station printed on your booking; trackwork can move it.

items.q: How much does a night train from Berlin cost?
items.a: Booked early: **seats from about EUR 30**, **couchettes from about EUR 59 to 69**, **beds in shared sleeper compartments from about EUR 49 to 99**, and private compartments well above that. Fares are dynamic like flights, and **Nightjet and EuroNight bookings open about 6 months ahead**, so the cheap categories go first.

items.q: Can I use the Deutschlandticket or a rail pass on night trains?
items.a: **The Deutschlandticket is not valid on any night train**; these are long-distance services. **Interrail and Eurail passes work, but every night train needs a paid seat or berth reservation** booked with the operator, and popular dates sell out before the pass discount matters.
